docs.title: checkOwners
docs.text:
checkOwners infers who knows each part of a repository from its git history, then compares that with the CODEOWNERS file you committed. The repository is smusali/checkowners.

It reads git locally, sends nothing anywhere without a token, and never phones home. Network use is opt-in GitHub API access.

docs.title: A five-minute audit
docs.text:
Git 2.23.0 or newer is required, and the clone needs full history.

pip install checkowners
checkowners audit

uvx checkowners audit runs the same thing without installing. A bare checkowners runs audit, and the exit codes are in Exit codes.

docs.title: In CI
docs.text:
The composite Action needs a full clone; a shallow checkout fails before analysis starts.

permissions:
  contents: read
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    with:
      fetch-depth: 0
  - uses: smusali/checkowners@v0
    with:
      comment_on_pr: false

Inputs, outputs, permissions, and the SARIF upload are in GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Write CODEOWNERS
docs.text:
checkowners generate

The command fills the generated block and leaves a manual block alone. Where to go next:

  • Usage for every command, every config key, and CI.
  • Methodology for the signals, the formulas, and the limits.
  • Privacy for what is read, stored, and sent.
  • FAQ for tokens, teams, identity, and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

Each dated heading is the UTC calendar day that version was published to PyPI. Unreleased has no date.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• A documentation site is published from this repository, with search and a version per release.
  • A bare checkowners runs audit, and checkowners --help still prints help.
  • checkowners doctor reports configuration rows and --env adds the environment, where a missing token is unverifiable and not a pass.
  • checkowners report --html FILE writes one offline HTML report: an overview, a treemap, an ownership map, a timeline, and a drill-down.
  • checkowners diff SPEC reports the ownership impact of a diff, and suggest --diff SPEC or suggest --pr N routes a reviewer for it.
  • --diff-only SPEC limits the read-only analysis commands to the paths a diff touched without replacing the cached map.
  • checkowners simulate --remove @alice reports the paths that lose coverage and the truck factor before and after, from the cached map.
  • simulate --remove-file takes a list of identities, and --remove-status takes every cached owner with one contributor status.
  • checkowners graph --export writes DOT, GraphML, GEXF, or JSON, and reports articulation points, orphan files, and a transfer path.
  • checkowners topology reports weighted Louvain clusters with modularity and cross-seed stability, and compares them with declared teams.
  • checkowners onboard PATH lists inferred onboarding steps, following resolved imports where they exist and naming the missing signals.
  • checkowners suggest recommends one reviewer from expertise and current load, and names the load signal it measured.
  • checkowners sync opens or updates one reconciliation pull request; --commit commits locally and --dry-run prints the diff.
  • identity merge, identity unmerge, and identity audit record or report identity changes, and contributors.roster sets each status.
  • drift, risk, and validate accept --format text|json|sarif|junit, and the Action uploads the SARIF and JUnit files.
  • The Action upload_sarif input uploads that SARIF, publishes workflow annotations, and completes a check run named checkOwners.
  • .github/workflows/checkowners.yml is a reusable workflow wrapping the Action with the same inputs.
  • policy chooses which findings block: drift, a single expert, unowned paths, and incomplete analysis warn, and an invalid owner fails.
  • generate keeps a # checkowners:manual block byte for byte, and output.block_order decides which block wins an overlapping path.
  • generate and validate take --dialect github|gitlab, and GitLab writes one section per top-level directory.
  • Incremental analysis replays a usable baseline by default, and --no-incremental scores the full lookback again.
  • Blame results are cached between runs, --verbose prints hit and miss counts, and --no-cache skips the cache.
  • History follows renames and copies by default, under analysis.follow_renames and analysis.rename_similarity.
  • Recency uses each path's median commit gap as its half-life, and each owner reports expertise and a continuity status.
  • Change survival is a scored signal: current blame lines over that person's lines at their last commit.
  • Co-authored-by trailers credit co-authors when git.count_co_authors is true, and analyze reports the merge strategy it saw.
  • Drift compares a team rule with the expanded member set and says whether the inferred owners are inside it.
  • Drift severity scores owner overlap, confidence delta, path criticality, decay, and a single qualified owner, with configurable cutoffs.
  • qualified-owners reports a criticality-weighted distribution of top-owner share, and an empty criticality map says so.
  • Per-path risk measures concentration over every score above the threshold, while top_n_owners caps only the displayed list.
  • risk reports former_knowledge_share, the share of score held by owners the roster marks as former.
  • cache info reports this repository's id and state file, exiting 1 with no state file and 2 outside a repository.
  • .checkowners-baseline.json is excluded by default, so refreshing the accepted-findings file is not itself a finding.
  • RepositoryAnalyzer is the library entry point, and its stored observations can be scored again with no second git pass.
  • The Action caches pip downloads and ~/.checkowners, reusing a restored map only when its commit and config hash match.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Every cache is keyed on the package version and the configuration hash, so a release or a config change refreshes it.
  • trends reports historical_activity_confidence instead of avg_top_confidence, because the two are not the same measurement.
  • The review signal reads closed pulls in batched queries, and a window cut short by the request budget lowers analysis completeness.
  • The Action fail_on_drift input defaults to empty, so a run follows policy.drift.fail and blocks only on a novel finding.
  • The GitHub API features need only a token; there is no separate extra to install.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• The version: key and the model.ownership, model.risk, and model.topology pins are gone, and each now exits 2 naming the line.
  • schema_version and models are gone from every JSON payload, which now carries checkowners_version alone.
  • The github extra is gone; checkowners[all] is now checkowners[graph].
  • The command aliases who, bus-factor, decay, and balance are gone; use owners, qualified-owners, risk, and suggest.
  • analysis.max_owners, analysis.exclude_bots, and the flat scoring: section are gone, replaced by one key each.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• expertise --json validates against the published schema, which did not accept the confidence field it emits.
  • Path globs and paths.exclude treat \ and / alike and stay case-sensitive on every operating system.
  • Git path output is read as UTF-8 with quoting disabled, and Git older than 2.23.0 exits 4 naming the version to install.
  • Concurrent handle-cache writes take a lock, so two commands on one repository cannot corrupt the cache.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• certifi is pinned to 2026.10.19, which drops the compromised emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root (GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2).
  • PyJWT and urllib3 are pinned past the advisories that the previous pins carried.
Correctness and trust: scored ownership, privacy controls, and supply-chain checks. Inference stays local git.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Ownership scoring renormalizes over the available signals into ownership_score on [0, 1], with evidence_quality reported separately.
  • Analysis completeness is a run-level score with analysis_gaps, and --fail-on-incomplete exits 3 when a bound left the run short.
  • --json emits a documented schema with checkowners_version, repository, head_sha, generated_at, and completeness.
  • Privacy controls add output.anonymize, output.aggregate_only, privacy.redact_emails, identity.mode, and contributors.exclude.
  • On-disk state uses tokenized emails and locked atomic writes, with cache path|info|clear|purge and a 256 MiB cap.
  • checkowners baseline create writes accepted findings, so --baseline keeps CI failing only on findings outside that file.
  • suppressions accepts explicit, reason-required exceptions, which drift and audit honor alongside the baseline.
  • checkowners explain PATH decomposes one path's inferred ownership and checkowners owners PATH prints the ranked list.
  • checkowners explain-path PATH shows the winning CODEOWNERS rule and the whole match chain.
  • Analyze excludes linguist-generated and linguist-vendored paths and reports how many each mechanism dropped.
  • Blame honors .git-blame-ignore-revs, ignores whitespace, detects moves, and omits commits above git.mass_refactor_file_fraction.
  • .mailmap is applied first when identity.mailmap is true, and analyze reports whether a mapping file was found.
  • generate and sync fail when the re-resolved owners differ from the intended set, unless output.verify_round_trip is false.
  • generate warns at 2 MB, refuses above output.max_bytes without --force, and reports the bytes and rules it wrote.
  • generate and sync refuse a broad * rule that would assign different owners, unless output.allow_broad_patterns is set.
  • .pre-commit-hooks.yaml exposes checkowners-validate and checkowners-drift.
  • Human reports, the job summary, and comments state that this is a knowledge-risk tool and not a performance measure.
  • Each GitHub Release carries a CycloneDX SBOM and a signed build-provenance attestation.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Every command shares the exit codes 0 clean, 1 internal, 2 usage, 3 findings, 4 integration, and --exit-zero clears only 3.
  • The Action output checkowners_drift is now drift_summary, in both github-action --json and GITHUB_OUTPUT.
  • The composite Action runs checkowners github-action once for drift, qualified owners, decay, the job summary, and GITHUB_OUTPUT.
  • Recency, decay, and lookback age against --as-of, else SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, else the HEAD committer time, never the wall clock.
  • An offline score is no longer capped at 0.85, so a value means the same thing with or without a token.
  • The default qualification.strategy is adaptive, so commit count is shrunk evidence; threshold keeps the old eligibility gate.
Corrective release: identity, Action supply chain, and metric naming. No new inference behavior.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The Action input max_output_entries caps each list in the output summaries, and the full payloads are always uploaded as an artifact.
  • The Action installs the checkowners version matching its own tag, and a release whose pins disagree is rejected.
  • Third-party Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs.
  • checkowners/py.typed ships in the wheel, so type checkers see the annotations.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The truncated owner count is named qualified_owner_count, because the old name claimed a simulation it never performed.
  • The Action mode input defaults to commit, matching the configuration default.
  • The all extra composes the other extras instead of duplicating their pins.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The Action comment lookup paginates past 100 comments, so it updates its own comment instead of posting a new one.
  • The Action no longer fails on a fork pull request or a read-only token; it writes the report to the job summary.
  • The Action exports GITHUB_TOKEN on every CLI step, and sets CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR to a writable path.
  • A solo-maintainer repository no longer receives a per-file knowledge-risk comment that names every path.
  • Multiline Action outputs use a random delimiter, so report text cannot break GITHUB_OUTPUT.
Pattern-aware drift, per-repository state, and local identity resolution.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• A real CODEOWNERS pattern engine: * within a segment, ** across segments, a leading / anchored, last match wins.
  • generate consolidates per-file inference into directory rules when every file under a directory agrees.
  • generate and sync refuse to overwrite a hand-written CODEOWNERS unless --force is passed.
  • --version prints the version, and a bare checkowners prints help.
  • GitHub noreply addresses resolve to @handles with no token and no network.
  • A persistent email-to-handle cache remembers both hits and misses, so a repeat run does not re-query.
  • Several commit emails that resolve to one handle become one owner, with the commits summed.
  • Drift results carry notes explaining a comparison it skipped, such as raw emails against @handle rules.
  • A progress bar on stderr during the blame pass, on a terminal only.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Drift matches inferred files against real patterns, so a directory rule no longer marks the files under it missing.
  • State is keyed per repository, so two checkouts of one remote share a map and unrelated repositories never do.
  • Analyze runs blame in parallel and skips unowned files.
  • validate follows GitHub's actual rules, including relative patterns and inline comments.
  • validate --json exits non-zero on an invalid file, matching the text output.
  • sync is a no-op success when the generated file already matches the committed one.
  • Review-coverage and review-load scans are bounded to the 200 most recent pulls.
  • trends counts distinct commits per period, so one commit touching twelve files counts once.
  • The default exclusions cover package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, and the generated CODEOWNERS itself.
  • The Action fails fast with a clear message on a shallow clone.
  • PyGithub moved from a hard dependency into an extra.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • The drift.compare_to option is gone; it was parsed and documented but never read.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Generated CODEOWNERS never emits a [...] character range, which GitHub does not support.
  • Terminal output renders a path such as [companyId] verbatim instead of interpreting it as markup.
  • A review-load suggestion can no longer propose shifting reviews onto someone who is already overloaded.
  • Graph DOT export escapes quotes and backslashes in node ids and labels.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• checkowners github-action runs the whole CI flow and writes the drift, qualified-owner, and decay summaries to GITHUB_OUTPUT.
  • checkowners trends [--periods N] [--period-days D] reconstructs one snapshot per period from a single git log pass.
  • The review-activity signal is populated when github.api_enabled is set and a token resolves.
  • The Action posts a drift and qualified-owner comment on pull requests, which comment_on_pr controls.
  • A serialized graph cache per repository, invalidated by the analysis timestamp.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• paths.exclude adds *.generated.* by default.
  • The Action honors its config and mode inputs through CHECKOWNERS_CONFIG and CHECKOWNERS_DRIFT_MODE.
  • Qualified-owner tiers respect the configured bus_factor thresholds instead of hardcoded ones.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • .checkowners/ is git-ignored, so a cache of contributor emails cannot be committed when the state directory is inside a repository.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Confidence scoring on every path and owner pair, from commit recency, commit frequency, blame coverage, and review activity.
  • A per-path qualified owner count with candidate backup reviewers, as checkowners qualified-owners [PATH] [--all].
  • Continuity-risk detection that separates a dormant owner from a departed one and names a transfer target.
  • An ownership graph behind the graph extra, rendered in the terminal or exported to DOT.
  • checkowners expertise PATH ranks the evidence for one path.
  • checkowners topology infers collaboration clusters and reconciles them with declared GitHub teams.
  • checkowners suggest detects an overloaded reviewer and proposes a redistribution.
  • checkowners onboard PATH walks from broad ownership to deep expertise and emits a checklist.
  • A persistent state cache, with CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR to move it.
  • A composite GitHub Action with the drift, qualified-owner, and decay outputs, plus an example workflow.
  • Drift severity tiers from the worst confidence delta plus the concentration and decay signals.
  • The configuration sections scoring, decay, and bus_factor, plus confidence_threshold and github.api_enabled.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• analysis.lookback_days defaults to 365, and analysis.top_n_owners to 3.
  • paths.exclude adds node_modules/** by default.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• checkowners drift compares inferred ownership with the committed CODEOWNERS and reports what disagrees.
  • checkowners sync writes the inferred file, and checkowners validate checks the committed one.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • The package metadata and entry point work from a clean install.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • checkowners analyze, checkowners print, and checkowners generate infer ownership from git history and write a CODEOWNERS file.

docs.title: Contributing to checkOwners
docs.text: checkOwners is a pure-git ownership inference engine. This guide covers the local workflow, the conventions CI enforces, and the pull-request process.

docs.title: Picking work
docs.text: Start from a good first issue or any open issue. Every planned change is an issue labeled for the release it ships in, and its blocked-by list names what has to merge first. Usage questions go to Discussions.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/smusali/checkowners.git
cd checkowners
uv sync --frozen --all-extras --group dev

Dependencies come from uv.lock, and every command below runs inside that environment.

Command What it does uv run pytest the whole suite uv run pytest tests/test_analyze.py one test file uv run pytest -k "test_name" the tests matching a substring uv run ruff check . lint, including the S and PTH rules uv run ruff format . format uv run mypy types, --strict from pyproject.toml uv build produce the sdist and wheel in dist/

The documentation site uses the docs group:

uv sync --frozen --group docs && uv run mkdocs build

Optionally install the hooks so ruff, formatting, and mypy run on every commit, plus checkowners validate when CODEOWNERS changes and checkowners drift on push:

uv run pre-commit install

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Fork["Fork"] --> Branch["Topic branch"]
  Branch --> Push["Push"]
  Push --> PR["Open a PR"]
  PR --> CI["CI runs"]
  CI --> Review["Review"]
  Review --> Merge["Squash and merge"]

Name the branch after the change, keep commits focused, and open the pull request against main. The description states the user-visible behavior change, links the issue, and names follow-up work that is intentionally out of scope. Squash and merge is the default, so granular commits inside a branch are fine.

Commits follow Conventional Commits: feat, fix, docs, chore, ci, or test, with a module name or an umbrella area as the scope. The body explains why.

CI runs pytest on Ubuntu for Python 3.11 to 3.15 plus macOS and Windows on the newest, each with the runner's Git. Pushes to main, the nightly schedule, and a manual run add every operating system for every Python, plus Ubuntu with Git 2.23.0 and 2.39.3. CI then builds the wheel, exercises the CLI against it, and runs ruff and mypy --strict.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 to 3.15, and Git 2.23.0 or newer at runtime because blame ignore-revs landed there. An older Git exits 4 and names the version it found.
  • Functional style. The classes are dataclasses, frozen where they can be.
  • A type hint on every signature; mypy --strict is enforced over src, tests, and tools.
  • Paths are pathlib.Path, which ruff PTH enforces.
  • A new command lives in one of the cli/ modules, takes --json, and persists through state.write_state when that makes sense.
  • Ownership is never binary: an owner carries an ownership_score and a separate evidence_quality.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Each module has a tests/test_<module>.py, and the CLI suite lives in tests/cli/.
  • Tests run the real CLI against a real temporary git repository built by the git_repo fixture, with author and committer dates pinned.
  • unittest.mock appears only at the GitHub HTTP seam, checkowners.github.request, through the fake_api fixture, and at the comment-on-PR urlopen seam.
  • Tests that touch the cache set CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR so they never write the contributor's real state.
  • Property tests use Hypothesis, which runs 200 examples by default.
  • filterwarnings = ["error"] is on, so a new warning fails the suite.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Runtime dependencies are capped at the next untested major (typer>=0.9.0,<1, rich>=13.0.0,<16, and so on); raise a ceiling when CI proves the new major. uv.lock pins the development, docs, and tools groups with hashes across Python 3.11 to 3.15. requirements.lock holds the runtime set alone, exported with uv export --no-dev --no-emit-project --extra graph, because the composite Action installs it with pip --require-hashes. Regenerate both in the commit that changes a dependency.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
Removing a command, changing the JSON schema, the scoring model, the default policy, an Action input or output, or the configuration schema is a breaking change. A 0.x minor release may include one when the changelog calls it out; 1.x keeps those contracts stable until a major release. 1.0 additionally means external production users and outside contributors, not a star count.

Add user-visible notes under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md as they merge, one line each.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
One tagged GitHub Release produces the artifacts; nothing publishes from main on its own.

  1. Set __version__ in src/checkowners/__init__.py.
  2. Move [Unreleased] to a dated ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD heading, using the UTC day of the PyPI release.
  3. Keep the Action pin, the committed wheel, and both lockfiles on that version. tools/check_changelog.py rejects a tag whose pins or heading disagree.
  4. Publish the release as vX.Y.Z. The workflow checks the changelog, runs uv build, publishes with a GitHub OIDC token, writes a CycloneDX SBOM, attests the distributions, and uploads the SBOM and provenance.
  5. The docs workflow deploys that version and points latest at it.

docs.title: Governance
docs.text:
Samir Musali (@smusali) is the only Core Maintainer and the only person with release rights. The second maintainer seat is open. The rungs are Contributor (a merged change), Reviewer (repeated review in an area), Maintainer (can merge there), and Core Maintainer (release rights, and changes to these rules).

The code of conduct covers behavior, and the architectural decisions are in Methodology.

Changes here may be written with agent assistance. Every one of them is human-reviewed, tested, and signed off before it merges.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text:
Open an issue from the issue chooser: the bug form for a defect, the wrong-owner form when inference named the wrong owner, the feature form for a proposal. Each asks for the command, the configuration without tokens, the repository shape, and the merge strategy.

Supported versions and how to report a vulnerability are in the security policy.

docs.title: Does checkOwners need a GitHub token?
docs.text:
No. The inference is pure git and runs offline. A token only adds three features: resolving non-noreply emails to @handles, resolving teams and subteams, and the review signal with team reconciliation. Without one you still get scored ownership, drift, qualified owner counts, freshness, and onboarding, and the remaining signal weights are renormalized so the score stays on [0, 1].

Noreply addresses such as login@users.noreply.github.com resolve to @login with no token at all.

docs.title: Where does the token go?
docs.text: In the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, and nowhere else. github.token in checkowners.yml is refused, because that file is committed and a secret there would be published. In Actions the composite Action exports the job token for you; pass github_token only when you need a PAT or App token.

docs.title: What permissions does each feature need?
docs.text:
Capability Job token Fine-grained PAT Email to @handle the default token is enough no extra repository permission Teams and subteams not available; the job token cannot list org teams Organization members: Read Review coverage, suggest pull-requests: read Pull requests: Read Pull-request comment pull-requests: write Pull requests: Write Code scanning upload security-events: write Code scanning alerts: Read and write Check run checks: write Checks: Read and write sync pull request contents: write and pull-requests: write Contents and Pull requests: Read and write

A fork pull request cannot comment or upload code scanning results: GitHub makes that token read-only whatever the permissions: block says. The Action skips both, writes the report and the SARIF artifact, and does not fail the job.

docs.title: Will the generated CODEOWNERS use handles or emails?
docs.text: Handles whenever one was resolved. A path whose owners are still raw addresses is skipped rather than written with an address, because GitHub would not understand it. Writing a .mailmap is the cheapest way to improve this.

docs.title: Does it handle teams and subteams?
docs.text: With a token, github.org, and github.resolve_teams, yes. checkOwners loads the organization team list once, follows child teams, and reports a team rule as aligned, partially drifted, unverifiable, invisible, empty, or nested. team_coverage is the share of inferred handles who are members.

docs.title: Can a report leave out people's names?
docs.text: Yes. output.anonymize replaces each person with a stable person- token, output.aggregate_only drops per-person fields and keeps path and repository metrics, and privacy.redact_emails replaces addresses with tokens. generate and sync exit 2 under those settings, because a CODEOWNERS file has to name accounts.

docs.title: Can CODEOWNERS live in the repository root?
docs.text: Yes. checkOwners reads .github/CODEOWNERS, CODEOWNERS, and docs/CODEOWNERS, in that order, and writes back to whichever it found.

docs.title: Where is the cache?
docs.text: ~/.checkowners, or %USERPROFILE%\.checkowners on Windows. Set CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR to move it, checkowners cache path to print it, and checkowners cache purge to delete everything in it.

docs.title: How do I turn checkOwners on without failing on everything?
docs.text: Run checkowners baseline create and commit the file. Later runs then fail only on findings that are not in it. --exit-zero is the other way: it turns the findings exit code into 0 after printing the report.

docs.title: What is the difference between a baseline and a suppression?
docs.text: A baseline is a snapshot of what was already there, written by a command, and it ratchets: a finding you fix cannot come back silently. A suppression is a hand-written rule in the config that always applies, and it requires a reason so the next reader knows why.

docs.title: How do I fail only on critical drift?
docs.text: Leave policy.drift.fail false and branch on the Action's drift_summary, which carries the severity. A workflow step that fails when severity == "critical" is three lines of if:.

docs.title: Why is analysis completeness below 100% on a healthy repository?
docs.text: Completeness counts the evidence catalog, not the health of the repository. Without a token the review signal is missing; without a .mailmap or a .git-blame-ignore-revs file those corrections did not run. Each of those is a gap, so a normal run sits below 1 and still exits 0.

docs.title: Why did a formatter commit not take ownership?
docs.text: Commits that touch at least git.mass_refactor_file_fraction of tracked files are left out of blame, and revisions in .git-blame-ignore-revs are ignored. Both exist so a sweeping reformat does not become ownership.

docs.title: Why are some paths missing from analyze?
docs.text: They were excluded: linguist-generated or linguist-vendored in .gitattributes, a paths.exclude pattern, a deleted file, or a path whose only authors are bots.

docs.title: Can I keep a hand-written rule when I generate CODEOWNERS?
docs.text: Yes. Wrap it in # checkowners:manual:start and # checkowners:manual:end. generate rewrites only the generated block. output.block_order decides which block wins an overlap, and the later block is the winner.

docs.title: generate stopped on a marker error and left the file alone.
docs.text: The manual and generated markers are unbalanced or interleaved. The message names the line. Nothing is written until they pair up, so no manual rule is ever lost to a half-written file.

docs.title: generate refused because the file is too large.
docs.text: output.max_bytes defaults to 2.5 MB because GitHub ignores a CODEOWNERS file over 3 MB. Raise the limit, or let output.consolidate collapse uniform directories, or pass --force.

docs.title: networkx is not installed but I want graph.
docs.text: pip install "checkowners[graph]". The graph, topology, and onboarding commands need it; nothing else does.

docs.title: Is this a performance-measurement tool?
docs.text: No. It measures where knowledge is concentrated, which is a property of a repository, not of a person. Using it to evaluate individuals is unsupported and harmful.

docs.title: Does it use an LLM?
docs.text: No. Inference is deterministic git analysis, and the scoring code is in the repository to read.

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
checkOwners scores each (path, owner) pair from the git evidence it was able to collect, then compares the top owners of a path with the CODEOWNERS rule that covers it.

flowchart LR
  Git["Git history"] --> Signals["Five signals"]
  Reviews["Review API"] -.-> Signals
  Signals --> Score["ownership_score"]
  Signals --> Quality["evidence_quality"]
  Score --> Shares["Knowledge shares"]
  Score --> Drift["Drift severity"]

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
Signal Source Weight Reliability Recency exp(-ln 2 * days_since_last_commit / half_life) 0.30 1.0 Frequency commits / (max_commits_for_path + prior), prior 3 under adaptive 0.20 1.0 Blame porcelain lines for that person over total lines 0.20 1.0 Reviews reviews on pulls closed inside the review lookback 0.15 1.0 Change survival current blame lines over that person's lines at their last commit 0.15 1.0

Recency proxies whether someone still works here, frequency how often they touch the path, blame how much of the current text is theirs, reviews the knowledge that reading code produces, and change survival whether their work outlived them.

ownership_score  = sum(wi * ai * si) / sum(wi * ai)
evidence_quality = sum(wi * ai * ri) / sum(wi)

ai is 1 when the signal was observed for the path and 0 otherwise, so a missing signal is skipped rather than scored as zero and the range stays [0, 1] either way. A person with 0% blame still has that signal available: that is a measured zero. evidence_quality is the separate question of how much of the configured weight was actually collected, and it is never folded into the score. Two owners can share a score and differ in quality.

Under the default adaptive recency strategy the half-life is the path's median gap between commits, clamped to the floor and ceiling. Under fixed it is the configured half_life_days for every path. The score is a ranking signal, not a calibrated probability.

Each owner also reports active_expertise (their last commit, decayed), historical_expertise (their commits over their commits plus later commits by others), and maintenance_recency (the path's last commit, decayed). Continuity risk is a status rather than a day count: stable, inactive, superseded, or departed.

docs.title: Knowledge concentration
docs.text:
Concentration is computed over every score at or above the confidence threshold, before the display list is truncated to top_n_owners. Let pi be each owner's share of the score mass on one path:

  • top_owner_share is max(pi).
  • effective_owners is 1 / sum(pi^2), the inverse Herfindahl index.
  • hhi is sum(pi^2) and shannon_entropy is the entropy of pi in nats.
  • truck_factor_50, truck_factor_75, and truck_factor_90 are the smallest counts of highest-share owners whose shares reach each configured quantile.
  • a major contributor holds at least 0.05; minor_contributor_share is the rest.

qualified_owner_count is a different number: the owners at or above the threshold in the list already truncated to top_n_owners. It is a capped count, not a truck factor, and raising top_n_owners raises it without any code changing hands. The repository truck factor, reported by simulate, greedily removes the author who still covers the most files until covered files drop below the first truck-factor threshold.

docs.title: Drift severity
docs.text: Each drift entry scores 0.40 * the non-overlap between declared and inferred owners, 0.25 * the confidence delta capped at 1, 0.15 * the path criticality, 0.15 when the entry is decayed, and 0.05 when the qualified owner count is 1. Overlap is team_coverage for a team rule and the Jaccard overlap otherwise, so a superset of the declared owners scores below a disjoint set at the same delta. The default cutoffs are 0.15, 0.35, 0.55, and 0.75 for info, low, medium, high, and critical, and the command severity is the worst entry.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• analysis completeness: the fraction of the evidence catalog a run collected.
  • baseline: an accepted-findings file, so later runs fail only on new findings.
  • candidate backup reviewer: another scored person on a path, after the primary owners.
  • confidence delta: the clamped gap between declared and inferred owners on one path.
  • criticality: a configured weight in (0, 1] for a path glob, used when aggregating.
  • critical-path risk: the criticality-weighted mean of top_owner_share.
  • drift: the comparison of inferred owners with the committed rules.
  • knowledge at risk: the share of criticality weight on paths at or below the critical threshold.
  • load signal: what a review-load report measured: recorded reviews, a git authorship proxy, or an external provider.
  • last match wins: the last matching CODEOWNERS pattern assigns the owners.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• ownership_score ranks; evidence_quality reports collection. Neither is a probability, and an unobserved signal is unavailable rather than zero.
  • Pattern matching follows GitHub CODEOWNERS semantics in one engine, which generate, validate, and drift share. GitLab sections are a dialect on that engine, not a second matcher.
  • Identity resolution is local first and search last. Search relabels one address and never merges two owners.
  • Blame is git blame --line-porcelain, one process per path on a thread pool, cached by blob SHA. A replacement has to match porcelain line attribution.
  • There is no webhook. The Action writes bounded summaries and the calling workflow, which already holds the secrets, delivers them.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Git history is not complete expertise, and squash merges hide authors who are absent from the commit and its trailers.
  • Blame can over-credit formatting changes, which is what the ignore-revs file and the mass-refactor filter exist to reduce.
  • CODEOWNERS may differ from history on purpose. Drift is a question, not a verdict.
  • Team analysis, review evidence, and handle resolution for non-noreply addresses need a GitHub token.
  • Identity resolution can be ambiguous, and a user-search hit can attach the wrong account.
  • Trend scores use recency and frequency only, so they are not ownership_score.
  • Repository evidence cannot prove formal ownership, decision authority, operational or incident responsibility, employment, or reviewer availability. Inferred clusters are a hypothesis, not an org chart.

docs.title: Built on
docs.text:
• The repository truck factor in simulate, after Avelino, Passos, Hora, and Valente, "A Novel Approach for Estimating Truck Factors" (ICPC 2016).
  • The comparison of truck-factor algorithms, after Ferreira, Valente, and Ferreira (ICPC 2017), which is why simulate reports the coverage line rather than a degree-of-authorship estimate.
  • Counting reviews as knowledge, after Fritz, Ou, Murphy, and Murphy-Hill (ICSE 2010) and Fritz, Murphy, Murphy-Hill, Ou, and Hill (TOSEM 2014). checkOwners does not compute degree of knowledge.
  • Louvain community detection for topology, which is exploratory.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
This is a knowledge-risk tool, not a performance-measurement tool. Using it for individual evaluation is unsupported and harmful.

checkOwners reads git history on the machine where it runs and writes an ownership map. Email addresses are stored as tokens. When identity lookup is enabled, an address that is not already resolved may be sent to the GitHub user-search API. contributors.exclude keeps those people out of that lookup.

output.anonymize, output.aggregate_only, privacy.redact_emails (--redact-emails), identity.mode, and contributors.exclude control what reports may show. See Privacy controls.

suggest is the report most likely to be misused for individual evaluation. It names people only to recommend a reviewer. output.anonymize replaces those names with person- tokens. output.aggregate_only drops names, the recommendation, and per-person load fields, and keeps load_signal plus path-level review_concentration and divergence. Do not use either form in a performance review.

docs.title: What is read
docs.text:
All of this stays on the machine that runs the command:

  • git log and git blame (history and line attribution, not a copy of the source tree)
  • .mailmap, .git-blame-ignore-revs, and .gitattributes
  • the CODEOWNERS file, if one exists
  • .github/checkowners.yml

Source file contents are not uploaded. The cache key is the normalized origin URL, or the absolute checkout path when the repo has no origin.

docs.title: What leaves the machine
docs.text:
With --offline, or with no GITHUB_TOKEN, nothing does. The command prints:

Network access: disabled
Review evidence: unavailable
Team verification: unavailable

Otherwise a token can be used for the calls below. Each one runs only when its gate is on and the token is set. --offline skips all of them. Noreply addresses, .mailmap, and an existing handle file still resolve locally.

When Call Sent github.resolve_handles is true (the default), a local commit SHA is known, and no earlier stage resolved the address GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha} The commit SHA. The response used is author.login, author.type, and committer.type The commit read found no login. A core rate-limit gap does not continue to this row GET /rate_limit, then GET /search/users with query {email} in:email The address is the search query. Search is last github.org is set and a token exists GET /orgs/{org}/members once per analyze The organization name. The response is member logins. A failure leaves membership unused github.api_enabled is true and GITHUB_REPOSITORY is set. Review collection also resolves handles, so the search row above can run first Ownership review: POST /graphql for closed pulls in the review window, including reviewer logins and changed paths. suggest still uses GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls (closed, newest update first, at most 200), then GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/files, and reads open pulls the same way, at most 200 Repository name. Responses are reviewer logins, requested reviewers, and changed paths generate or sync with github.resolve_teams and github.org, or topology and explain when github.api_enabled and github.org are set GET /orgs/{org}, GET /orgs/{org}/teams, GET /orgs/{org}/teams/{slug}/members Organization name. Responses are team slugs and member logins Composite Action, comment_on_pr true, same-repo pull request GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/comments, then POST a new comment or PATCH the existing one The report markdown checkowners sync without --commit or --dry-run, when the generated file differs GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}, Git Data reads and writes for one commit on checkowners/reconcile-codeowners, then GET, POST, or PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls Repository name, the CODEOWNERS text, and the pull-request body.

A workflow that posts GITHUB_OUTPUT to a webhook does that itself. checkOwners does not open that connection. See Data flow.

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text:
Location Contents ~/.checkowners/state/<id>.json Inferred owners, the analyzed commit, and a history baseline of commit SHAs, path lists, and blame line counts. The baseline does not store author addresses. Email addresses on the ownership map are email: tokens: email: plus the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 over the lowercased address. ~/.checkowners/graph/<id>.json Serialized ownership graph for that analysis. Contributor emails in node ids are the same tokens. ~/.checkowners/handles/<id>.json This repository's email token to GitHub @handle. A hit stores the handle, the source, and the account type. A miss stores an empty handle and the UTC instant it expires. A legacy string handle is still a hit. A legacy empty string is dropped. @handles are stored as themselves. ~/.checkowners/identity/<id>.json Contributor records for merges and unmerges. Emails are tokens. Handles stay handles. ~/.checkowners/handles.json Legacy global handle file. It is not copied into the per-repository files. cache purge deletes it.

checkowners cache path prints the directory. CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR overrides it. The composite Action sets that variable to ~/.checkowners when cache is "true", and to ${{ runner.temp }}/checkowners-state when cache is "false". Analysis does not upload file contents. With cache "true", the Actions cache stores the directory for the next run.

The cache holds hashed emails and @handles. It does not hold raw addresses after the next read. Those identities are still personal data.

docs.title: Deleting it
docs.text:
checkowners cache clear removes analysis state and graph files and leaves handle files and the identity graph in place.

checkowners cache purge removes every file under the cache directory, including per-repository handle files, the identity graph, and a legacy handles.json. That is how you delete this data. The cache directory itself is kept.

docs.title: Disable identity lookup
docs.text: Set github.resolve_handles: false, or pass --offline. Noreply parsing and .mailmap still run locally when mailmap is enabled. --offline also skips review coverage and team verification.

docs.title: Redact emails
docs.text: Set privacy.redact_emails: true, or pass --redact-emails. Addresses in output are replaced with email: tokens. The other presentation controls are in Privacy controls.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
There is no time-to-live.

State and graph files are dropped oldest-first once they exceed 256 MiB together. Handle files and the identity graph are not part of that eviction. They stay until cache purge, or until you delete the cache directory.

--max-age SECONDS refuses to reuse an analysis older than that. It does not delete the file. 0 expires immediately for reuse. Omit the flag for no age limit.

A job that uses the Action's runner temp directory loses the cache when the runner is discarded. CLI and hand-rolled CI keep ~/.checkowners/ until you purge it, unless you point CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR at an ephemeral path.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Git["git history"] --> Score["Scoring"]
  Ids["Identity API"] -.-> Score
  Reviews["Review API"] -.-> Score
  Teams["Team API"] -.-> Score
  Score --> Local["Terminal and files"]
  Score --> Outputs["Action outputs"]
  Score --> Comment["PR comment"]

The dotted edges are optional and gated. Git history is the only required input, and every output below is written by checkOwners itself; a webhook is posted by the caller's workflow from the Action outputs.

Identity resolution is local first: a configured identity, .mailmap, GitHub noreply addresses, then this repository's handle file. A commit lookup sends a SHA and reads author.login and account type. User search still sends the email and is last. Org membership is one members request when github.org is set. Review coverage and team resolution are API steps and run only under the gates in What leaves the machine. Outputs are the terminal, local report files, GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the pull-request comment. A webhook is optional and is posted by the caller's workflow from GITHUB_OUTPUT, not by checkOwners. output.aggregate_only drops identities from identity audit and leaves duplicate_count.

docs.title: Threat model
docs.text:
What source data is read? Git history, blame, mailmap, ignore-revs, gitattributes, CODEOWNERS, and .github/checkowners.yml. Source file contents are not uploaded.

What leaves the machine? Nothing under --offline or with no token. Otherwise the calls in What leaves the machine: an unresolved email on user search, repository and pull-request metadata for review coverage, organization and team membership for team resolution, and the report body when the Action comments.

When is GitHub contacted? Only when a gate above is on and GITHUB_TOKEN is set. Local noreply parsing, mailmap, and cache hits do not contact GitHub.

What is cached? The ownership map, the ownership graph, and the handle map, under ~/.checkowners/ or CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR.

Does the cache contain sensitive identities? Yes. Emails are email: tokens, not raw addresses. @handles are stored in full. Treat the directory as personal data.

Where is it stored? On the machine that ran the command. The Action uses the runner temp directory. Do not commit the cache. This repo's .gitignore ignores .checkowners/.

How are tokens handled? The only supported token source is the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable. github.token in config is rejected because that file is committed. See SECURITY.md.

What permissions are required? The per-feature permissions are in the FAQ, and the workflow blocks are in GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Every command, every configuration key, and the CI integration. The scoring model is in METHODOLOGY.md and common questions are in FAQ.md.

This is a knowledge-risk tool, not a performance-measurement tool. Using it for individual evaluation is unsupported and harmful.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
analyze reads git history once and caches a map every other command reads.

flowchart LR
  Git["Git history"] --> Analyze["analyze"]
  Analyze --> State["Cached map"]
  State --> Generate["generate"]
  State --> Drift["drift"]
  State --> Risk["risk"]
  State --> Suggest["suggest"]
  Generate --> File["CODEOWNERS"]
  Drift --> Report["CI output"]

The map lives at ~/.checkowners/state/<repo-hash>.json, keyed by the normalized origin URL so two checkouts of one remote share a file, or by the absolute path when there is no origin. CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR moves the cache. A command reuses the map when its commit is HEAD and the config hash and package version match; otherwise it analyzes again, replaying the stored baseline since that ref and reusing blame for unchanged blobs, which matches a full lookback for the same repository, commit, and config.

Global flags go before the command name, as in checkowners --allow-stale risk:

  • --allow-stale reuses a map whose commit is not HEAD.
  • --max-age SECONDS refuses a map older than that; 0 expires immediately.
  • --no-cache neither reads nor writes the cache.
  • --no-incremental scores the full lookback and writes a fresh baseline.
  • --offline makes no network call.
  • --as-of ISO8601 fixes the instant recency and decay are scored against.
  • --redact-emails replaces addresses in output with stable tokens.
  • --diff-only SPEC limits read-only analysis to the paths a diff touched.
  • --exit-zero turns exit 3 into 0 after the report is printed.
  • --fail-on-incomplete exits 3 when run completeness is below 1.
  • --verbose prints blame cache hits and misses.

cache info reports sizes and this repository's state file, cache clear deletes analysis state, graph files, and blame files, and cache purge deletes everything including handle files and the identity graph. Those files are evicted oldest first above 256 MiB together.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command What it does audit Every doctor row plus inference: drift, concentration, decay, unowned paths. Bare checkowners runs it doctor Configuration rows: branch, file size, syntax, access, teams, coverage. --env adds the environment analyze Infer ownership scores, qualified owner counts, and continuity-risk warnings print Print the inferred map to stdout generate Write CODEOWNERS ordered by ownership score validate Validate the committed CODEOWNERS syntax explain-path PATH Show which rule owns a path, and the whole match chain explain PATH Decompose the inferred scores. --why-not and --owner narrow it owners PATH The ranked owner list, and nothing else expertise PATH Evidence ranking for one path from the cached map drift Compare the committed file with the inferred map; severity and the worst score delta baseline create Write an accepted-findings file so later runs fail only on new findings sync Open a pull request proposing CODEOWNERS changes. --commit commits locally risk Rank paths by composite knowledge risk qualified-owners [PATH] [--all] Per-path qualified owner count with candidate backup reviewers simulate --remove @alice What breaks when those people leave, from the cached map suggest Recommend a reviewer from expertise and current load. --diff and --pr scope it to a change diff SPEC Ownership impact for the paths changed in base...head graph [--export FORMAT] Render the ownership graph as dot, graphml, gexf, or json topology Louvain clustering of collaboration. Exploratory, not an org chart onboard PATH Inferred onboarding suggestions. Exploratory trends Historical activity and qualified owner count over time report --html FILE Write one offline HTML report identity audit \| merge \| unmerge Inspect and edit the contributor identity graph cache info \| path \| clear \| purge Inspect and delete the on-disk cache github-action Run the whole CI flow and write GITHUB_OUTPUT

graph, topology, and onboard need the graph extra.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
.github/checkowners.yml, every field optional, defaults shown. An unknown key exits 2 and names the line.

analysis:
  lookback_days: 365          # integer days, or adaptive for all history
  review_lookback_days: 365   # positive integer; omit to follow lookback_days
  min_commits: 1
  top_n_owners: 3
  confidence_threshold: 0.3   # owners below this are dropped from CODEOWNERS
  respect_gitattributes: true # linguist-generated and linguist-vendored first
  max_runtime_seconds: 300    # stop blame here and mark the run incomplete
  max_git_workers: 16
  max_api_requests: 2000
  follow_renames: true
  rename_similarity: 50       # percent, 1 to 100

qualification:
  strategy: adaptive          # adaptive | threshold
  min_commits: 1              # this key wins over analysis.min_commits
  strong_blame_override: 0.5  # adaptive keeps authors at or above this share

model:                        # every signal takes weight and reliability
  signals:
    recency:
      weight: 0.30
      strategy: adaptive      # adaptive | fixed
      half_life_days: 90      # the fixed half-life, and the fallback
      half_life_floor_days: 14
      half_life_ceiling_days: 730
      reliability: 1.0
    frequency: {weight: 0.20, reliability: 1.0}
    blame: {weight: 0.20, reliability: 1.0}
    reviews: {weight: 0.15, reliability: 1.0}          # needs api_enabled
    change_survival: {weight: 0.15, reliability: 1.0}  # needs blame

bots:
  exclude: true
  additional: []              # extra addresses or handles treated as bots

decay: {threshold_days: 180, alert_on_decay: true}

bus_factor: {critical_threshold: 1, warn_threshold: 2}

criticality: {}              # path glob to weight in (0, 1]; first match wins

risk: {truck_factor_thresholds: [0.50, 0.75, 0.90]}

paths:
  exclude: ["*.lock", "dist/**", "vendor/**", "node_modules/**", "CODEOWNERS"]

output:
  header: "# Generated by checkOwners. Do not edit manually."
  include_unowned: false
  include_confidence: false   # append "# alice(0.92) bob(0.71)" to each line
  consolidate: true           # collapse a uniform directory into one dir/ rule
  max_bytes: 2500000          # refuse to write more without --force
  verify_round_trip: true     # re-resolve every generated path
  allow_broad_patterns: false
  anonymize: false
  aggregate_only: false
  block_order: manual-first   # manual-first | generated-first

drift:
  mode: commit                # commit | repo | both
  min_confidence_delta: 0.2
  hysteresis_runs: 1          # hold a severity flip until N consecutive runs
  baseline_file: ""
  severity_thresholds: [0.15, 0.35, 0.55, 0.75]

suppressions: []              # explicit and reason-required

github:
  org: ""
  resolve_handles: true
  resolve_teams: true
  api_enabled: false          # gates the review signal and the API features

git:
  blame_ignore_revs_file: .git-blame-ignore-revs
  detect_moves: true          # pass -M and -C to git blame
  mass_refactor_file_fraction: 0.5  # 0 disables; omit these commits from blame
  count_co_authors: true
  co_author_weight: 1.0       # credit per trailer, against the author's 1
  merge_strategy: auto        # auto | squash | merge | rebase

identity:
  mailmap: true               # the cheapest identity fix
  mode: handle                # handle | email | hashed
  negative_cache_ttl_days: 30 # 0 stores no miss
  do_not_merge: []            # pairs that stay two owners

identities: {}                # "@alice": {emails: [], aliases: [], service_account: false}
privacy: {redact_emails: false}
contributors:
  exclude: []
  roster: {}                  # "@bob": former | active | inactive | bot | external

policy:
  drift:                      # also single_expert, incomplete_analysis, unowned
    fail: false
    severity: warning         # error | warning; error blocks when fail is omitted
  invalid_owner:
    fail: true
    severity: error

security:
  paths: []                   # empty applies the stricter rules to nothing
  minimum_effective_owners: 2
  require_declared_owner: true
  require_active_expert: true

policy.drift covers stale and changed, unowned covers missing, unowned-file, and observed-unowned, single_expert covers single-expert, and invalid_owner covers invalid-owner, owner-permission, invisible-team, empty-team, and file-size. With both set, fail decides the exit and severity is what the report shows. A path under security.paths blocks when its effective owner count is below minimum_effective_owners, when it has no declared owner, or when no owner is stable. The token is never read from this committed file: github.token is rejected, so set GITHUB_TOKEN.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Role CHECKOWNERS_CONFIG Config path, relative to the repository root or absolute. Wins over .github/checkowners.yml CHECKOWNERS_DRIFT_MODE commit, repo, or both. Wins over drift.mode CHECKOWNERS_BASELINE Accepted-findings path. Wins over drift.baseline_file CHECKOWNERS_STATE_DIR Cache root. Wins over ~/.checkowners GITHUB_TOKEN The only supported token source GITHUB_REPOSITORY owner/repo for the review, topology, and suggest API features GITHUB_OUTPUT github-action writes bounded summaries here SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH POSIX seconds used as the analysis instant when --as-of is omitted

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text: Scoring is a pure function of the repository, the commit, and the config. Recency and decay age against one resolved instant, never the wall clock: --as-of, then SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, then the HEAD committer timestamp. JSON carries head_sha and generated_at, and git log is pinned to that instant, so the same commit scored twice is byte identical.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
A .mailmap at the repository root is the cheapest accuracy fix: git already collapses one person's addresses, and checkOwners applies that first, offline. Commit emails then become GitHub @handles in this order:

  1. An entry under identities, which wins over everything below.
  2. .mailmap, unless identity.mailmap is false.
  3. Noreply parsing, with no token and no network: 12345+login@users.noreply.github.com becomes @login.
  4. This repository's handle cache under ~/.checkowners/handles/. A miss is skipped for identity.negative_cache_ttl_days.
  5. The commit author login, when GitHub linked the commit to an account.
  6. The GitHub user-search API, which needs a token and can attach the wrong account.

--offline or an empty token skips the last two steps. Evidence quality is scaled once per fresh analyze: 1.0 for a certain link, 0.75 for an unresolved email, 0.5 for a search hit.

Each owner carries a contributor_status of active, inactive, unknown, former, bot, or external. contributors.roster wins, then a bot account type, then organization membership, then commit age; only the roster assigns former. identity audit lists probable duplicates, identity merge LEFT RIGHT INTO records a merge, and identity unmerge LEFT RIGHT keeps a pair apart.

docs.title: Privacy controls
docs.text:
These apply to terminal output, JSON, the graph export, the Action JSON, the job summary, and pull-request comments. generate and sync exit 2 under anonymize, aggregate_only, or identity.mode: hashed, because a CODEOWNERS file has to name accounts.

Setting Effect output.anonymize Replace each person with a person- token, stable within one repository output.aggregate_only Omit per-person fields; keep path and repository metrics privacy.redact_emails Replace addresses with email: tokens identity.mode handle, email, or hashed for how a person is named contributors.exclude Drop those people from analysis, reports, and export

Addresses are stored as email: tokens in the cache. Changing contributors.exclude, contributors.roster, identities, identity.do_not_merge, identity.negative_cache_ttl_days, or bots.additional invalidates that cache; the presentation settings do not.

docs.title: Drift
docs.text:
drift compares the inferred map with the committed CODEOWNERS using real CODEOWNERS semantics: * within a segment, ** across segments, a leading / anchored to the root, a trailing / matching directory contents, last match wins.

Category Meaning missing An inferred file no rule covers stale A rule whose pattern matches no tracked file changed A rule whose owners disagree with the inferred owners of its files

Owner comparison is case insensitive, and an owner-less rule counts as intentional coverage. When the comparison would be meaningless, for example raw emails against @handle rules, drift emits a note instead of a false positive.

A rule whose owners contain / is a team rule. With a token, github.org, and github.resolve_teams, drift loads the organization team list once and reports the team as aligned, partial-drift, unverifiable, invisible, empty, or nested. team_coverage is the share of inferred handles who are members.

Severity weights 0.40 * the non-overlap, 0.25 * the capped confidence delta, 0.15 * path criticality, 0.15 for a decayed entry, and 0.05 for a qualified owner count of 1, then takes the worst tier under drift.severity_thresholds; drift.hysteresis_runs holds a flip until the new tier repeats. drift --fix-plan prints suggested edits without writing the file, and a manual rule that disagrees with observed expertise is named for review rather than reported as changed.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Internal error 2 Configuration or usage error 3 Findings 4 Git or GitHub integration failure

Every command uses these, and any non-zero status fails a CI step. --exit-zero turns 3 into 0 after the report is printed, and --fail-on-drift or --no-fail-on-drift forces policy.drift.fail for one run.

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
name: checkowners
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  drift:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: smusali/checkowners@v0
        with:
          mode: both

fetch-depth: 0 is required: a shallow clone has no history to score. A comment needs pull-requests: write, a code scanning upload needs security-events: write with upload_sarif: true, and a check run needs checks: write. Fork pull requests skip the comment and use the job summary.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Role config .github/checkowners.yml Config file path mode commit Drift mode: commit, repo, or both include_bus_factor "true" Emit bus_factor_summary include_decay "true" Emit decay_summary include_balance "false" Emit balance_summary max_output_entries "50" Cap each list in the summaries fail_on_drift empty Override policy.drift.fail; empty uses the policy baseline empty Accepted-findings file comment_on_pr "true" Maintain one pull-request comment upload_sarif "false" Upload checkowners.sarif to code scanning python_version "3.13" Interpreter to set up checkowners_version the Action's pin Package version; empty uses the pin install_spec empty Local extras spec for this repository only index_url empty pip index for an internal mirror offline "false" Install the committed wheel with --no-index github_token the job token Exported as GITHUB_TOKEN cache "true" Cache pip downloads and ~/.checkowners

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: drift_summary, bus_factor_summary, decay_summary, and balance_summary are bounded JSON, and artifact_name names the artifact holding the full payloads. .github/workflows/checkowners.yml in this repository is a reusable workflow that wraps the same Action with the same inputs.

docs.title: Pre-commit
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/smusali/checkowners
    rev: v0.6.0
    hooks:
      - id: checkowners-validate   # on a CODEOWNERS change
      - id: checkowners-drift      # on push

docs.title: JSON contract
docs.text: Every --json command validates against schemas/commands.schema.json, JSON Schema draft 2020-12, one definition per command under #/$defs. Each payload carries checkowners_version, repository, head_sha, generated_at, and the analysis completeness.

docs.title: Adopting on a large repository
docs.text: Run checkowners audit and read the findings, then checkowners baseline create to accept what is already there, then add the Action with the default policy, which blocks only invalid owners. Fix findings over time and turn policy.drift.fail on at the end. suppressions is the explicit, reason-required escape hatch for a finding that should stay, and writing a .mailmap first is the single biggest accuracy win.
